sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Yogesh Kumar Gupta - advocate for the petitioner.
Shri Virendra Khadav appearing on behalf of Advocate Gen  ORDER Heard and perused the record.

2. This is second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 for grant of bail relating to Crime No.87/2024, registered at Police Station - Raipuriya, District Jhabua for offence under Sections 376(2)(n), 376(D), 344 of IPC, 1860.
The applicant is in custody since 03.06.2024.
His first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to file afresh after completion two month in custody, vide order dated 25.7.2024.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
Main accused Kamal has been granted bail by this Court vide order dated 16.7.2024, passed in MCRC No.25790/2024.
The case of the applicant is on better footing from the main accused.
The applicant is in jail since 3.6.2024.
Conclusion of trial will take a sufficient long time.
Under these circumstances, counsel prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
4. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the application and prayed for NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:29142 2 MCRC-42858-2024 its rejection.
5. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and custody period of the applicant, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant may be released on bail.

Consequently, without commenting on the merits of the case, second bail application filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148028783/
1 allowed.
6.

sentences.text: It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS.
7. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE girish Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148028783/
